chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all of them, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi Basir, who said:

"There is no objection to you increasing [the period] and her increasing [it] if the agreed term between you two has expired; you say, 'I have made myself permissible to you for another payment,' with her consent, and this is not permissible for another man until her waiting period (iddah) has ended." And likewise, whenever a man wishes to increase the period before the expiration of the term, he may not do so unless he gifts to her the remaining days that are still owed to her.

key_terms.الْأَجَلُ: The fixed term or duration of the temporary marriage contract.
key_terms.الْمُدَّةُ: The period or duration of the marriage.
key_terms.عِدَّتُهَا: The waiting period (iddah) a woman must observe after the marriage ends or expires before she can marry another.
key_terms.يَهَبُ: To gift or give as a present.

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for extending the duration of a temporary marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural distinction between renewing a *mut'ah* contract after its term expires versus extending it beforehand, a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding the flexibility of temporary marriage. It emphasizes that post-expiration renewal requires a new mutual agreement and consideration, whereas pre-expiration extension is treated as a gift of the remaining days, ensuring the wife's consent is explicit in both scenarios. This ruling underscores the contractual nature of *mut'ah*, distinguishing it from permanent marriage by allowing periodic renegotiation of terms.
